summary.headline: Meesho Q1 FY27: management says logistics cost per delivered order fell about ₹1 QoQ, and it guides to ~25% five-year NMV CAGR.
summary.overview: Management said fuel and minimum-wage hikes during Q1 FY27 were absorbed, with cost per delivered order down about ₹1 QoQ, and pricing rose at the same time as costs. NMV growth was about 2% QoQ, which management attributed to seasonality (Eid moved from Q1 last year into Q4) and a higher S&M spend base last year, not a change in the core business. Year-on-year AOV fell about 2% versus the roughly 5% annual baseline decline. New initiatives (Kirana Club, a low-cost local grocery logistics network) remain early and capped at about ₹200 crore annual EBITDA burn; Q1 operating loss was about ₹39 crore. The call also covered a GTA structure for middle- and last-mile logistics under VTPL and a Karnataka gig-worker fee, which management says is stayed and immaterial.

segments.name: Logistics (Valmo / 3PL)
segments.commentary: Valmo share of volumes about 50%, unchanged. Middle- and last-mile operations were moved into VTPL (GTA licence) from Q1, with first-mile and sort centres staying in Meesho Limited.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: About two-thirds of GMV-contributing sellers run ads; ROAS is similar to last quarter. Management does not disclose ad revenue share from Meesho Mall.

segments.name: New initiatives (Horizon 2)
segments.commentary: Q1 operating loss about ₹39 crore. Annual EBITDA burn cap is about ₹200 crore. Kirana Club is at early product-market fit, and the low-cost local logistics network is in experimentation for grocery, F&B and staples.

segments.name: Meesho Mall
segments.commentary: Growing faster than the overall platform, but management does not disclose its share of NMV.

guidance_outlook: Management expects logistics cost per delivered order to keep falling, with efficiency gains to show up in upcoming quarters and fuel and wage hikes described as small blips.
Long-term NMV growth baseline is about 25% CAGR over five years, higher in early years and lower later.
Q2 FY27 YoY growth will look lower because the festive Blockbuster Sale starts in October (Diwali moved to November). Q2 and Q3 combined should track the trajectory.
Contribution margin is expected to rise: logistics fee margin is being restored, efficiency gains are passed to sellers, and ad revenue improves.
AOV is expected to resume its decline as efficiencies are passed on.
capex_capacity: Logistics efficiency gains from sorters, locker delivery and lower RTO are cited, with all logistics operations now on a fully stabilised basis after the prior year's Q2/Q3 disruption.
Valmo share has no specific guidance; lanes go to the lowest-cost provider and volume-linked rate cards apply to 3PLs.
New initiatives are capped at an annual EBITDA budget of about ₹200 crore; the cap philosophy is unchanged.
demand_pricing: NMV grew about 2% QoQ. Management attributed this to seasonality, since Eid shifted from Q1 last year into Q4.
Year-on-year NMV per seller is down about 25% per the analyst, as merchant onboarding has grown fast. Management argues a larger seller base supports ad monetisation.
Annual frequency is up about 9% YoY on 29% ADU growth; older and newer cohorts both show rising frequency.
Management said competitive intensity has stayed high and has not changed in either direction, citing sub-platforms launched by others over the years.
For more than 50% of GMV-contributing sellers, Meesho is a primary income source, per internal surveys.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about the direction of logistics costs given fuel and wage increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects continued logistics cost reduction at a good pace. Cost per delivered order fell about ₹1 QoQ in Q1, offsetting the fuel and wage hikes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Valmo share, and what does the VTPL entity disclose?
qa_highlights.answer: Valmo share is about 50% and materially unchanged. VTPL houses only middle- and last-mile GTA operations, so its financials will not map directly to Valmo volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a change to the Horizon 2 burn cap, and what is it in absolute terms?
qa_highlights.answer: No change in philosophy. The annual EBITDA budget cap for new initiatives is about ₹200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the GST / GTA news flow, and what exposure exists?
qa_highlights.answer: The GTA model is used by other horizontal e-commerce players. Management says no regulator or tax authority has raised a query, and no SEBI communication has been received; it sees no material exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AOV stay flat sequentially, and what drives contribution margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases from fuel pass-through and raw-material costs offset the efficiency pass-through. Contribution margin is expected to rise as logistics fee margin is restored and ad revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Karnataka gig-worker fee exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: The court has stayed any action. Management provides for the cost conservatively in the P&L and says the amounts are not material.

risks_watch: Fuel and minimum wage inflation could return if the geopolitical or oil-price situation worsens.
The GTA/VTPL structure is under news-flow scrutiny from a proxy advisor. The matter has been referred to SEBI, though no communication has been received yet.
Q2 FY27 YoY NMV growth will look lower due to the festive sale timing shift, so monitor Q2 and Q3 combined.
Low-cost local logistics and Kirana Club are pre-product-market fit; the burn cap is ~₹200 crore per year.
NMV per seller is down about 25% YoY as the seller base expands; monitor ad monetisation per seller.
Karnataka gig-worker fee is stayed by court; provisions are held, and the amount is not material.
summary.management_tone: Confident on logistics cost trajectory and long-term opportunity, but evasive on Meesho Mall ad share and Valmo share, which it declined to quantify. Cautious on new initiatives, which it described as early and pre-product-market fit.
key_quotes: I think you should anticipate that we will continue to reduce our logistics cost at a very good pace, something that we have talked about even during the IPO.
So we've largely kind of offset this. Again, in the coming quarters, we expect to continue to gain efficiencies.
But I would say like there is no change as such in the competitive environment. It has stayed high and we will always expect it to stay high.

growth.why: Management reiterated a ~25% five-year NMV CAGR (higher early, lower later) and a ~5% baseline AOV decline, with cost-per-order down ~₹1 QoQ and ~2% QoQ NMV growth, but gave no specific capacity, orders or contracts behind the 25% target, so backing is vague.
